answer: A sybil swarm would need to replicate both the bond and computation per identity, while a gale of peer attestations flags duplicate behavior, and any nebula of cloned agents collapses once slashed bonds exceed the reward from forging identities. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique hardware-rooted key and complete a costly proof-of-work challenge seeded by a rotating atlas of epoch randomness. From once0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
